p: It is stated in the holy Zohar
on the verse "You shall dwell in sukkos
"And afterwards, 'they shall dwell in sukkos,' etc.
Rather, the first is for the guests,
the second for the people of the world, etc.
Fortunate is the portion of Yisrael,
דִּכְתִיב: כִּי חֵלֶק ה׳ עַמּוֹ וְגוֹמֵר
as it is written, 'For Hashem's portion is His people,' etc.
is the illumination of the seven holy middos
as is stated there in the holy Zohar:
כִּי שֵׁשֶׁת יָמִים עָשָׂה ה׳ וְגוֹמֵר.
'For in six days Hashem made,' etc."
And the souls of the seven shepherds
for his own middah in holiness, as is known.
the illumination of the seven holy middos
in all the souls of Yisrael.
For the aspect of the three holy Avos
is found in all the souls of Yisrael,
in that they are merciful, bashful, and doers of kindness.
is the middah of "kindness to Avraham,"
to do kindness with all creatures,
even with one who is not worthy;
and therefore dross came out of him.
"'So that His fear may be upon your faces'
And it is the aspect of contraction;
yet in this too there is dross.
the one in the middle, who joins the two middos,
to one who needs it and is worthy.
The aspect of Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
הַיְינוּ שֶׁהוּא רַבָּן שֶׁל כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל
is that he is the teacher of all Yisrael
and imparted the Torah to them.
Regarding the aspect of Aharon HaKohen,
it was said at Matan Torah (Shemos 19:6):
"And you shall be a kingdom of kohanim";
for so it was set in the souls of Yisrael,
that they be servants performing the holy service,
"And you shall be called kohanim of Hashem."
By the aspect of Yosef HaTzaddik
And the aspect of Dovid HaMelech, peace be upon him,
is the heart of all Yisrael,
"The heart in the body is like a king in a country."
And he is "the man raised on high,"
עוּלָּהּ שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה (עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה ה, א),
who raised up the yoke of teshuvah (Avodah Zarah 5a),
and he is the aspect of Mashiach,
who is the individual who repents
for whose sake the whole world is forgiven;
that is, he will bring the way of teshuvah
into the hearts of the souls of Yisrael.
there is found such a soul
into the heart of the totality of the souls of Yisrael.
And the illumination of the seven holy middos —
it is within the power of all the souls of Yisrael
because they are all a G-dly portion from Above.
And on this the holy Zohar cites:
as it is written, 'For Hashem's portion is His people.'"
And through the holiness of the sukkah we merit
to have drawn into our souls
the illumination of the seven holy middos.
And to this alludes "You shall dwell in sukkos
seven days" — "the first is for the guests";
to have set firmly in our souls
Therefore the essence of the mitzvah of sukkah comes
שֶׁהֵמָּה עִיקַּר סִיבַּת הַחַיִּים שֶׁל הַנֶּפֶשׁ,
which are the main cause of the life of the soul,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה יִהְיֶה נִשְׁפָּע בָּנוּ
and through this there will be drawn into us
life from the illumination of holiness.
And regarding this the verse uses
"So that your generations will know," etc.,
and it does not use the wording "so that you will remember,"
as it says regarding Yetzias Mitzrayim
לְמַעַן תִּזְכּוֹר אֶת יוֹם צֵאתְךָ וְגוֹמֵר.
"So that you will remember the day of your going out," etc.
עַל כָּרְחֲךָ דְּאֵינוֹ כְּדֵי לִזְכּוֹר לְבַד,
Perforce it is not merely in order to remember,
because what is brought about through the mitzvah of sukkah
that is, the recognition and feeling of the heart,
in the inwardness of the heart,
of the illumination of His holiness, blessed be He.
And to this the holy Zohar alludes:
that is, the illumination from Above
that is drawn into all the souls of Yisrael
through the mitzvah of dwelling in the sukkah.
alludes to the preparation for this
on the part of the soul,
which comes only by way of emunah,
as in the saying, "He is Truth,
that is, His illumination, blessed be He,
to shine the light of all seven
into the heart: the truth of His providence, blessed be He.
And the aspect of Knesses Yisrael,
that is, all the souls of Yisrael together —
only from the aspect of emunah,
to receive the illumination from Above
Men of the Great Assembly instituted that we say
Certainly the season is set apart for this
just as Pesach is "the time of our freedom,"
since we went out of Mitzrayim,
and Shavuos is "the time of the giving of our Torah,"
that they learned this from the wording of Scripture:
for regarding Pesach the Torah mentions
no expression of rejoicing at all,
only "And you shall make a Pesach to Hashem your G-d"
whereas regarding the festival of Shavuos it says
(ibid. 11), "And you shall rejoice before Hashem your G-d."
For on Pesach, although they had
the illumination of His countenance, blessed be He,
nevertheless, because it was only for the moment
and was at once concealed from them,
when the process of Yetzias Mitzrayim was completed
"And you shall rejoice before Hashem your G-d";
that is, from this rejoicing is born in the heart,
since it brought us all the way before Him, blessed be He.
And as is known, in all the holy convocations
from then on for all generations,
when this time arrives each year.
וְהִנֵּה בְּחַג הַסּוּכּוֹת נֶאֱמַר גַּם כֵּן
Now regarding the festival of Sukkos it also says
"And you shall rejoice before Hashem your G-d
seven days" — with the four species.
to come before Him, blessed be He,
וְעַל זֶה אָנוּ מְשַׂמְּחִים לְפָנָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ
and for this we rejoice before Him, blessed be He,
as stated in the Midrash (Vayikra Rabbah 30:2):
"Whoever takes the palm branches in his hand —
אָמְנָם עוֹד יֵשׁ נוֹסָף בְּחַג הַסּוּכּוֹת
Yet there is more added regarding the festival of Sukkos:
the expression "And you shall rejoice in your festival"
that is, a special rejoicing from Hashem, blessed be He,
by virtue of the holiness of the festival,
through the surrounding light of the mitzvah of sukkah.
And for this a special name was given
that it is called "the time of our rejoicing."
(Pesikta DeRav Kahana, the supplementary piska for Sukkos)
counts three times that an expression of rejoicing
is mentioned in the holy Torah
including also "And you shall be only joyful"
לְרַבּוֹת יוֹם טוֹב אַחֲרוֹן שֶׁל חַג
to include the last day of the festival
even the day of Shemini Atzeres —
from the root of the holiness of the festival of Sukkos,
that Shemini Atzeres is the absorption of
the holiness of the festival of Sukkos,
just as the festival of Shavuos is
the completion of the holiness of the festival of Matzos.
That is, from the joy of the holiness of Sukkos
the joy is set and absorbed
for all the days of the year.
And this is what is alluded to in the verse
that is, permanence and being are given
that is drawn down on this festival,
so that a small remnant remain
from which the impression will remain,
so that the joy be set in the heart
for all the days of the year.
